lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: handling conflict or a mistake professionally

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic handling conflict or a mistake professionally task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Given a short fictional workplace-mistake scenario (for example, sending something to the wrong recipient, or being late without notice), the learner rehearses reporting it out loud to a trusted adult playing the supervisor, using a three-part structure (what happened, what I'm doing about it, what I need), then revises based on feedback.
safetyNotes: No audio or video recording is made; the adult gives live feedback and the learner writes notes afterward.
The mistake scenario is fictional and does not require the learner to disclose or discuss any real mistake from their own life.

simulationAlternative.description: If no adult is available to role-play the supervisor, the learner writes both sides of the conversation as a short script, then reads only their own side aloud once and self-checks it against the same look-fors.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: In the fictional scenario, would it have been better to report the mistake sooner, and how would you recognize that same moment in a real situation?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Structure and clarity: The report includes all three parts clearly. | Responsiveness to feedback: The revised version reflects specific feedback that was given. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner practice a second, harder version: reporting a mistake that was only discovered by someone else first, not self-caught, using the same three-part structure adapted for that harder situation.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic handling conflict or a mistake professionally task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

localMaterials.label: paper or notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: handling conflict or a mistake professionally worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Given a short fictional workplace-mistake scenario (for example, sending something to the wrong recipient, or being late without notice), the learner rehearses reporting it out loud to a trusted adult playing the supervisor, using a three-part structure (what happened, what I'm doing about it, what I need), then revises based on feedback.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact handling conflict or a mistake professionally decision or action.
Model move 2: Before practicing, write down what makes reporting your own mistake feel harder than reporting someone else's.
Model move 3: With your adult playing the supervisor, report the fictional mistake using the three-part structure.
Model check: Structure and clarity: The report includes all three parts clearly. | Responsiveness to feedback: The revised version reflects specific feedback that was given.

resources.title: handling conflict or a mistake professionally action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for handling conflict or a mistake professionally.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: handling conflict or a mistake professionally coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Given a short fictional workplace-mistake scenario (for example, sending something to the wrong recipient, or being late without notice), the learner rehearses reporting it out loud to a trusted adult playing the supervisor, using a three-part structure (what happened, what I'm doing about it, what I need), then revises based on feedback.
Coach direction: Before practicing, write down what makes reporting your own mistake feel harder than reporting someone else's.
Learner prompt: What is one reason reporting your own mistake might feel harder than pointing out someone else's?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: handling conflict or a mistake professionally complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult playing the supervisor, report the fictional mistake using the three-part structure.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I stated clearly what happened, without minimizing or over-explaining.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I stated what I was already doing about it.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I stated what I needed, if anything, from the supervisor.

Equal-access rule: If no adult is available to role-play the supervisor, the learner writes both sides of the conversation as a short script, then reads only their own side aloud once and self-checks it against the same look-fors.

resources.title: handling conflict or a mistake professionally minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: In the fictional scenario, would it have been better to report the mistake sooner, and how would you recognize that same moment in a real situation?
Success checks: Structure and clarity: The report includes all three parts clearly. | Responsiveness to feedback: The revised version reflects specific feedback that was given.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: handling conflict or a mistake professionally supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional handling conflict or a mistake professionally condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Structure and clarity: The report includes all three parts clearly. | Responsiveness to feedback: The revised version reflects specific feedback that was given..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
